behavior_in_task_description.explanation: This is a multimodal visual bug-fix task. The instruction gives the requirement in general terms: every object in the attached video must render in the position and orientation it was placed in, for any such node anywhere in the world and however it was turned. The video, which is the referenced spec, shows all five defects the hidden tests check: the canopy sitting off its trunk, upside-down apples and grass, the fence not joining the trunk, mirrored rail stubs on the Z-running leg, and the twisted gate. The p2p guards only check behaviour that already works and stays covered by 'render as placed'. No output files, interfaces or schemas are required beyond fixing the engine code.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: The hidden C++ unit tests drive the real MapblockMeshGenerator::generate(). There is one f2p test per visible defect: the scaled allfaces offset, the fence joining a facedir trunk, Z-direction rails, an upright plantlike node, and all 23 facedir rotations of a mesh node. P2P guards cover generalisation ('anywhere', 'however turned') and stop fixes that would break existing behaviour.

informative_test_structure.explanation: test_content_mapblock.cpp has a header explaining the approach, well-named helpers (MeshGenScene, Extent, sameBox, cellOf), and one descriptively named test per behaviour, each with a comment saying what it checks. Assertion messages print the geometry that was actually generated. test.sh and verifier.py are clearly sectioned.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: Bug patches are applied and deleted in the same RUN layer. Git history is wiped and re-initialised, so the upstream fix commit can't be reached. File timestamps are all set to one value so modification times don't point at the bugs. The agent has no network access. Tests and solution are not in the image, and test.sh restores src/unittest from harbor_base before applying the hidden tests. Scoring uses test outcomes only.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task is a C++ engine bug fix. No structured output is expected.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: Luanti is checked out at a fixed base commit and IrrlichtMt at a fixed commit hash. Only apt system packages are unpinned, which is acceptable. The tests use no pip packages.

typos.explanation: No typos were found in paths, commands, test names or identifiers. config.json and task.toml list the same f2p/p2p names as the TEST() registrations, and the asset paths match. Some template comments in test.sh still mention 'wx' from another task, but they are only comments and don't affect anything.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile copies only bugs/ (then deleted) and assets/recording.mp4. Neither tests/ nor solution/ is copied in.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: The image installs only build tools for the project, the repo's own unit-test build (part of the repo), python3 and ffmpeg/Xvfb for inspecting the video. The hidden test file is added and compiled at verification time by test.sh. No test-only frameworks are baked into the image.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies fix.patch, a real source-level fix for all four files: re-ordering translate/scale, correcting the connection directions, restoring the plantlike wallmount default, scoping the facedir rotation, and using degree-to-radian conversion. It does not echo outputs.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The agent fixes existing source code and produces no output files. The only referenced file, the input video, is named with its full path.
